name: Freshly reconnected account, no confirmed salary, two salary sightings: the steady rule credits it (G359)

expected.notes: Re-derived for G360 with the pay on the 1st (calendar month) and the salary mid-period, so the steady credit sits inside the window. Today is Thu 8 Oct 2026, payday Sun 1 Nov, 24 days away; the window is strictly before payday. The account was reconnected recently, so there is no confirmed salary stream. Balances: Barclays 200 + Starling 2,000 = 2,200 pooled. The salary 3,000 (two sightings, 15 Aug and 15 Sep, 31 days apart, equal amounts: monthly rhythm within tolerance, largest regular credit on Barclays, due before payday) is a steady salary, credited to Barclays on Thu 15 Oct (day 7). The mortgage 1,100 leaves Barclays on Fri 16 Oct (day 8). Left to spend: pooled 2,200, day 7 + 3,000 = 5,200, day 8 - 1,100 = 4,100; the lowest point is the opening 2,200, so Left to spend 2,200. Barclays walk: 200, day 7 + 3,000 = 3,200, day 8 - 1,100 = 2,100. After payments 2,100, low point 200 (the opening balance). Starling has no bills so it is not walked: after payments and low point are its balance, 2,000. Spend from is the smaller of after payments and low point: Barclays 200, Starling 2,000 (below the pool 2,200). Nobody is short: no cover move, at risk 0. The period is on day 8 (1 Oct is day 1), so there is no payday plan (companion.py:2558, days_into_period <= 3). G436 (Kevin 2026-11-07, every account in isolation, money in vs money out), which supersedes the Left to spend and Spend from figures worked above where they differ: Each account on its own: Barclays 200 + 3,000 (the steady salary, predicted and attributed) - 1,100 = 2,100; Starling 2,000. 2,100 + 2,000 = 4,100. The pooled low point (2,200) did not count the salary that lands mid-period; the closing figure does. Barclays' dip to 200 before it lands is only a warning. G481 (Kevin 2026-11-20), which supersedes the Left to spend and Spend from figures worked above where they differ: each account's Available = cash now - max(0, bills before payday - money in before payday); money in only offsets bills and never adds, and no timing is involved. Left to spend is the sum of the accounts, less plans on no account and the buffer (none here). Barclays: cash 200; bill 1,100 (mortgage, Fri 16 Oct); money in 3,000 (the salary, Thu 15 Oct, two sightings, so predicted): 200 - max(0, 1,100 - 3,000) = 200, the salary offsets the mortgage and adds nothing (it was 2,100). Starling Personal 2,000. Left to spend 200 + 2,000 = 2,200. After payments stay 2,100 (200 + 3,000 - 1,100), low point 200 (the opening); covered, no move, at risk 0.
